cap-define-product: Define what a product is made of: People and agents share one agreed map of what a product is made of, changed only on purpose.
fn-597: The map, at version 15, defines thirteen kinds in two layers, each with its properties, links, rules and a real example, answers 45 of its 47 questions, and logs each version.
fn-change-ontology: /edit-ontology changes only the kinds one need touches, with the product owner's typed yes at three points, ends only when the map reads valid, and lands through the change plays.
fn-ontology-in-every-project: The settings name the map by its place in memory, Phoenix memory holds version 15, the same as Garura's source, and each play's agent reads it through the memory tool.
fn-readers-in-step: Each part that describes or checks the model's shape follows the map's current version.
fn-check-model-on-change: Each change to the map shows the product owner what it breaks in the model, recorded as owed.
fn-model-shape-version: The model says which version it is built to, so Move the product model to the new version's shape (fn-move-model) knows which moves it needs.
fn-extend-ontology: A team adds its own kinds or rules to the map Garura provides, and changes the plays that read them with it.
fn-profile-decision-kinds: The profile and the product decision that the model already holds get their kinds, properties, links and rules in the map.
fn-approval-state-kind: The map names one approval state for every kind, and maps the states of today onto it.
cap-manage-model: Manage the model: A living map, added to, changed and pruned as work is done, and the source of what to try next.
fn-add-found-part: The keeper writes the page of a domain, capability or feature found while other work goes on, then its index entry, thin when it is thin, all or nothing.
fn-change-part: A part changes only from words a person approved: named lines, a whole page, an intent page, its one-line, its intents or its parent, by one edit standard.
fn-take-part-out: A part is taken out only on a person's named approval: an old intent repointed, an intent page removed, a capability merged or a slice removed.
fn-725: Each link follows the ontology's rules, is kept on both sides, and points at a part that exists.
fn-724: The ready check says for each part whether work can start, ready, partly ready or not ready, with its gaps, and the same model always gives the same answer.
fn-check-model: The structure check reads the model's pages and index for their shape and links on every change, as findings, never a stop.
fn-close-model-gaps: Loose parts, links on one side only, intents nothing serves and the same part written twice are found, and what the model can take is closed.
fn-726: From any intent, a person lists the parts and slices that serve it; from a domain, its intents and capabilities.
fn-part-approval: Each part says whether a person approved it, it changed, or it is in progress.
fn-model-moves-with-work: A design approval updates the model, and a change left for later is listed for Learn.
fn-index-through-skills: Every play adds, changes and takes out parts through the two index skills, not its own script.
fn-model-tool: One tool writes the model's pages and entries in the shape the ontology sets, with the plays and templates it lacks.
fn-try-next: The model proposes an idea with its evidence, a person confirms or drops it, and an experiment records what was tried and its result.
